title: Conditioning Terms for Grain Held Under Storage Agreements: What the Dryer Costs and What It Takes
content:
Grain above the programme's target moisture is dried before it is credited into store, and the member pays for the water taken out rather than for the time the dryer ran. These are the conditioning terms of Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Terms

**Points removed.** Points removed are the moisture read on the way in less the programme's target moisture, and a pass that would remove fewer than the programme's minimum points is billed at the minimum points rather than not at all.

**The charge.** The charge is the programme's rate per point per bushel, times the points removed, times the bushels through the dryer, and where that comes to less than the programme's pass minimum the pass minimum is charged instead.

**Shrink.** Shrink is taken on top of the charge and is not itself a charge: water leaving the grain and the handling loss together take bushels off what is credited into store, at the programme's handling shrink percentage for each point removed, and the bushels credited are the bushels after that.

**One pass, one ticket.** Drying and shrink are computed once per scale ticket; a load sent through the dryer twice carries two passes and two shrink lines, distinguished by the day each pass ran.

**Grain the member will not have dried.** Where the member declines drying the grain is not taken into store at all and is returned to them, because the elevator will not hold wet grain on the member's account.

## The two things a pass produces

| What it is | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| the drying charge | money owed on the storage account for the water taken out |
| the shrink | bushels off what is credited into store, at the programme's handling shrink percentage for each point removed |

The first is a charge and the second is not; the shrink never appears as money and the charge never appears as bushels.

## Worked pass, on hypothetical readings

Six thousand bushels are read in at 17.4 percent against a programme whose target is 14.5 percent and whose rate is 0.0450 for each point on each bushel. The points removed are the moisture read in less the target, which is 2.9 points, comfortably above the programme's minimum of 0.5 points. The charge is six thousand bushels multiplied by 2.9 points multiplied by four and a half cents, which is 783.00, and that stands well above the programme's pass minimum of 20.00, so 783.00 is what is charged.

At a handling shrink percentage of 0.50 for each point, the same pass takes six thousand bushels multiplied by 2.9 points multiplied by half of one percent, which is 87.00 bushels off what is credited into store; the member is credited with the bushels after that rather than with the bushels across the scale.

## Boundary case, on hypothetical readings

Grain read in at 14.8 percent against the same target of 14.5 percent stands 0.3 of a point above it. Three tenths is fewer than the programme's minimum points of 0.5, so the pass is billed on 0.5 points rather than on 0.3, and rather than not at all.
